title: Torsion etale-origin sheaves are acyclic for ph-to-big-etale direct image
statement:
Let $T$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $B_T=(\mathrm{Sch}/T)_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and $\pi_T:\mathrm{Sh}(B_T)\to\mathrm{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{Et}})$ be as in [lem-trf-big-small-etale-exact-retraction]. Use the big ph site $(\mathrm{Sch}/T)_{ph}$ [def-trf-ph-scheme-site] with the same underlying category and compatible universe presentations [def-weil-size-convention]. The identity functor from $B_T$ to $(\mathrm{Sch}/T)_{ph}$ induces a geometric morphism $\epsilon_T:\mathrm{Sh}((\mathrm{Sch}/T)_{ph})\to\mathrm{Sh}(B_T)$ [def-trf-geometric-morphism]; its direct image regards a ph sheaf as an etale sheaf, without changing its underlying presheaf. For every torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], set $G=\pi_T^{-1}F$. Then the ordinary adjunction unit $G\to\epsilon_{T,*}\epsilon_T^{-1}G$ is an isomorphism, and
$$R^q\epsilon_{T,*}(\epsilon_T^{-1}G)=0\qquad(q>0).$$
The higher direct images are the ordinary right derived functors on abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. No uniform integer annihilating $F$ and no invertibility condition on its torsion orders are assumed.

source.place: Tag 0DE4, lemma-V-C-all-n-etale-ph, part (1), with a_T=pi_T composed with epsilon_T; degree-zero unit from Tag 0DDW, lemma-describe-pullback-pi-ph; section-ph-etale defines epsilon_T.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-ph-etale-comparison-hypotheses] with base scheme $S=T$. Use $\mathcal C=\mathrm{Sch}/T$, $\tau=ph$, $\tau'=\mathrm{Et}$, $\mathcal P$ the proper morphisms, and $\mathcal A'_X$ the full subcategory of torsion small-etale-origin sheaves $\pi_X^{-1}F_X$. That node gives the inclusion of the etale topology in ph, the comparison morphisms with identity direct image, the weak Serre condition, and all five properties needed for the general comparison theorem. In particular it supplies proper base-change stability, stability under restriction, the ph sheaf condition, stability under every proper higher direct image, and the three-stage refinement of every ph cover. Thus none of these properties is being inferred just from a definition. The slice $\mathcal C/X$ is canonically the category of schemes over $X$: its objects are $U\to X\to T$, and its morphisms are exactly the $X$-morphisms. Its two induced cover structures are the big ph and big etale cover structures on $X$ because both are defined on the underlying families of scheme morphisms. All these sites use the compatible presentations in the item.

source.place: Tag 0F0I, lemma-compare-ph-etale, and section-ph-etale; the hypotheses of Tag 0EZF are written out in the cited comparison-hypotheses node.

proof.text: The given $F$ is a torsion abelian sheaf on $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$, so $G=\pi_T^{-1}F$ belongs to $\mathcal A'_T$ by its definition in [lem-trf-ph-etale-comparison-hypotheses]. Property (3) of that node says that the underlying presheaf of $G$ is already a ph sheaf. The same node describes $\epsilon_T^{-1}$ as ph sheafification and $\epsilon_{T,*}$ as leaving the presheaf unchanged. Sheafification of an already ph sheaf has its canonical unit invertible: by the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] its identity factors through that unit, and uniqueness makes the factor and unit mutual inverses. Consequently the particular map $G\to\epsilon_{T,*}\epsilon_T^{-1}G$ in the statement is an isomorphism. This proves the asserted unit, rather than an unspecified isomorphism between its source and target.

source.place: Tag 0F0I, lemma-compare-ph-etale, Property (A-sheaf), proved there using Tag 0DDW, lemma-describe-pullback-pi-ph.

proof.text: Let $H=\epsilon_T^{-1}G$. By $G\in\mathcal A'_T$, this $H$ lies in the full subcategory $\mathcal A_T$ defined as the inverse-image class in [lem-trf-refined-topology-comparison-vanishing]. Apply that theorem to the data verified in Step 1, and take its slice object $X$ to be $T\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}T$. It gives $(V_n)$ for every integer $n\geq0$: $R^i\epsilon_{T,*}H=0$ for $1\leq i\leq n$. For an arbitrary $q>0$, take $n=q$ and $i=q$. The resulting equality is exactly $R^q\epsilon_{T,*}(\epsilon_T^{-1}G)=0$. These are ordinary right derived functors on abelian sheaves by the cited theorem's convention. The hypothesis package uses all locally torsion sheaves, so neither choosing $n=q$ nor applying the theorem imposes a common annihilator or an invertibility assumption.
